301: Kaya-chan Isn't Scary by Yuritaro (Seven Seas) is a horror comedy with a tough little heroine. Chie is a kindergarten teacher who keeps noticing that one of her students, the stone-faced Kaya, reacts to things no one else can see. Kaya can see evil spirits, and she deals with them by fighting back. It's a fun pick for readers who like spooky stories with a big helping of laughs.
305: The Fox and Little Tanuki by Mi Tagawa (Tokyopop) is a gentle fantasy about growing up. Senzou, a powerful black fox spirit, has been locked away for misbehaving. To earn his freedom, the Sun Goddess makes him mentor Manpachi, a small and very eager tanuki who wants to serve the gods. The grumpy fox and the cheerful little tanuki make a sweet pair, and it's a great choice for younger readers and families.
306: Animal Crossing by Kokonasu Rumba (Viz Media) is a lighthearted comedy based on the Nintendo game. The story follows a new arrival who moves to a deserted island and starts building a life there with a cast of animal neighbors. Each chapter brings small adventures, silly misunderstandings, and island projects. It's a cheerful, easy read for kids and for any fan of the games who wants more time on the island.
308: Raven of the Inner Palace by Kouko Shirakawa (Seven Seas) is a historical fantasy mystery light novel. Deep inside the emperor's inner palace lives the Raven Consort, a woman who never visits the emperor and is rumored to have strange powers. When the young emperor Gao Jun comes to her with a request, she is pulled into secrets she would rather avoid. It's a quiet, atmospheric read for fans of court intrigue and ghostly mysteries.
309: Ninja Slayer by Bradley Bond (Vertical) is a cyberpunk action story with a wild sense of style. In the neon city of Neo-Saitama, an ordinary salaryman loses his wife and son when they are caught in a battle between ninja. Dying, he is possessed by a vengeful ninja soul and rises as Ninja Slayer, sworn to kill every ninja he can find. It's fast, violent, and deliberately over the top, made for readers who enjoy bold action.
310: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind by Hayao Miyazaki (Viz Media) is a sweeping fantasy set long after a war that wrecked the world. A toxic jungle filled with giant insects is spreading across the land, and Nausicaä, the young princess of a small valley, studies it while others fear it. When war comes to her people, she is drawn into the conflict. It's a thoughtful, beautifully drawn story that goes much deeper than the film.
311: Aria The Masterpiece by Kozue Amano (Dark Horse) is a calm, gentle slice-of-life story. On a terraformed Mars now called Aqua, the city of Neo-Venezia is famous for its canals. Akari Mizunashi arrives there to train as an Undine, a gondolier who guides tourists through the city. Each chapter follows her small discoveries and friendships, making it a soothing read for anyone who enjoys cozy, low-stakes stories.
313: A Galaxy Next Door by Gido Amagakure (Kodansha) is a sweet romantic comedy. Ichiro Kuga is a young manga artist working hard to support his little brother and sister. When he needs an assistant, he hires Shiori Goshiki, a calm and lovely young woman who turns out to have a very unusual secret. It's a warm story about family and first love, perfect for readers who like gentle romance.
314: A Polar Bear in Love by Koromo (Yen Press) is a cute comedy romance. A polar bear meets a little seal and falls head over heels in love at first sight. The seal, though, is sure the bear is just trying to eat him and spends every moment terrified. The misunderstandings keep piling up in short, funny chapters, making this a sweet pick for animal lovers and fans of light comedy.
315: A Returner's Magic Should Be Special by Wookjakga (Yen Press) is a fantasy action manhwa. Desir Arman is one of the last survivors fighting the Shadow Labyrinth, a disaster that destroys the world. When he fails, he wakes up thirteen years in the past, just as he is about to enter magic school. He sets out to use what he knows to change the future. It's a good fit for fans of time-loop stories and magic academy adventures.
316: Spy Classroom by Takemachi (Yen Press) is a spy action comedy. Klaus, a brilliant spy, is put in charge of a team for a mission so dangerous it is called impossible. The catch is that his team is made up of seven girls who all flunked out of spy school, and Klaus is a terrible teacher. Lots of twists and teamwork make it a fun read for fans of heist and spy stories.
318: Mink by Megumi Tachikawa (Tokyopop) is a bubbly sci-fi comedy. Mink is an ordinary middle school girl who dreams of becoming a famous idol. When she gets her hands on a strange gadget from the future, she can transform into a glamorous cyber idol. Keeping her double life a secret turns out to be harder than she expected. It's a light, fun read for fans of magical girl and idol stories.
320: Gannibal by Masaaki Ninomiya (Ablaze Manga) is a tense horror thriller. Police officer Daigo Agawa transfers to Kuge, a remote mountain village, with his wife and young daughter. The villagers seem friendly, but Daigo soon hears rumors that the powerful family who controls the area eats people. As he digs deeper, the village grows more threatening. It's a slow-burn, unsettling read for fans of dark mysteries and rural horror.
325: Girls' Last Tour by Tsukumizu (Yen Press) is a quiet sci-fi story set at the end of the world. Chito and Yuuri are two girls traveling through the ruins of an empty city on a small tracked vehicle, searching for food, fuel, and whatever is left. They have little but each other, but they find small joys along the way. It's gentle, thoughtful, and a little melancholy, perfect for readers who enjoy reflective stories.
326: Gokurakugai by Yuto Sano (Viz Media) is a stylish supernatural action story. In Gokurakugai, a rough walled-off part of town, Tao and Alma run a troubleshooting office that will take almost any job. Many of those jobs involve the Magai, monsters that prey on people. Sharp art, a lively setting, and an easygoing partnership make this a strong pick for fans of demon-hunting action series.
327: Gold Digger by Fred Perry (Antarctic Press) is a fun action adventure comic with a manga style. Gina Diggers is a genius scientist and archaeologist who loves exploring ancient ruins and finding treasure. She travels with her adopted sister Brittany, a werecheetah warrior with a big heart and a bigger punch. Together they get into trouble with magic, monsters, and science. It's a lively pick for fans of fantasy adventure with plenty of humor.
328: My Hero Academia: School Briefs by Anri Yoshi (Viz Media) is a lighthearted light novel set in the world of My Hero Academia. The stories take place at U.A. High School between the big fights, following Class 1-A through dorm life, school events, and everyday moments. Readers get to see Deku and his classmates relax and goof around. It's a fun bonus for fans of the series who want more time with the characters.
331: The Demon Girl Next Door by Izumo Ito (Seven Seas) is a sweet fantasy comedy. Yuko Yoshida wakes up one morning with horns and a tail and learns that she comes from a line of demons. Her family is cursed with poverty, and the only way to break the curse is to defeat a magical girl. The problem is that Yuko is not very strong. It's a cozy, funny read for fans of gentle comedies.
332: The Elder Sister-Like One by Pochi Iida (Yen Press) is a supernatural romance. Yuu is a lonely boy who has lost his parents and is living with relatives who don't want him. When he finds a strange book and summons a demon, she takes on the form of an older sister and decides to look after him. The story is warm and a little odd, a good pick for readers who like slow, tender relationships.
333: Attack on Titan: Junior High by Saki Nakagawa (Kodansha) is a school comedy spin-off of Attack on Titan. Eren, Mikasa, Armin, and the rest of the cast are now students at a junior high that is shared with the Titans. Eren still holds a grudge against the Titans, but this time the battles are over lunch and school clubs. It's a goofy, affectionate parody for fans who want to see the characters in a lighter setting.
338: Hell Girl by Miyuki Eto (Del Rey) is a supernatural horror series told in short stories. Rumor says that if you enter a name on a website at midnight, the Hell Girl will send that person to hell. The price is that your own soul will go there too when you die. Each chapter follows someone pushed to the edge and deciding whether revenge is worth it. It's a dark, moody read for fans of spooky anthologies.
344: Hirano and Kagiura by Shou Harusono (Yen Press) is a sweet boys' love romance. Kagiura is a first-year student who gets a new roommate in the school dorm, the third-year Hirano. Living together, the two grow close, and Kagiura begins to realize his feelings run deeper than friendship. It's a gentle, slow-building story set in the same world as Sasaki and Miyano, a good fit for readers who enjoy soft romance.
347: Nyankees by Atsushi Okada (Yen Press) is an action comedy about stray cats. In a quiet neighborhood, the local cats are divided into rival gangs who fight for territory, just like teenage delinquents in a classic gang story. The cats have names, codes of honor, and big personalities, and their brawls play out like a school-yard showdown. It's a funny and unexpectedly exciting read for cat lovers and fans of tough-guy stories.
357: Bobobo-bo Bo-bobo by Yoshio Sawai (Viz Media) is a wildly silly action comedy. In the future, the evil Chrome Empire sends its Hair Hunters to shave everyone bald. Standing against them is Bobobo-bo Bo-bobo, a man with a huge blond afro who fights with the strange art of the Nose Hair Fist. The jokes are random, loud, and nonstop. It's perfect for readers who love absurd humor and parodies of fighting manga.
360: Captive Hearts by Matsuri Hino (Viz Media) is a romantic comedy with a fantasy twist. Megumi Kuroishi is a rich teenager whose family has served the Tokino family for generations because of an ancient curse. When Suzuka, the Tokino daughter, comes back into his life, the curse takes hold and Megumi finds himself compelled to serve her. It's a sweet, playful romance from the creator of Vampire Knight.
361: Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon? Familia Chronicle: Episode Lyu by Fujino Omori (Yen Press) is a fantasy action spin-off of DanMachi. Lyu Leon is a quiet elf who works as a waitress at the Hostess of Fertility tavern in Orario. This story looks back at her past as an adventurer with the Astrea Familia, a group devoted to justice. It's a great pick for DanMachi fans who want more of Lyu's story.
367: Pokémon Adventures: Gold & Silver by Hidenori Kusaka (Viz Media) is an all-ages adventure set in the Johto region. Gold is a boy from New Bark Town who would rather play than go on a journey. That changes when a mysterious trainer named Silver steals a Pokémon from Professor Elm's lab, and Gold sets out to catch him. It's a fast, exciting story for young fans of the games and anyone who loves Pokémon battles.
369: Pretty Face by Yasuhiro Kano (Viz Media) is a romantic comedy with a ridiculous setup. Rando Masashi is a tough karate fighter who is badly hurt in a bus accident. The doctor who rebuilds his face uses a photo from his wallet, and Rando wakes up looking exactly like Rina, the girl he has a crush on. Soon he is living with her family, pretending to be her missing twin. It's a goofy, fast-paced comedy.
372: Tougen Anki: Legend of the Cursed Blood by Yura Urushibara (Yen Press) is a supernatural action series. Shiki Ichinose is a rebellious teen who learns that he carries the blood of oni. When the descendants of Momotaro, the legendary oni slayer, come to hunt him down, his life is turned upside down. He heads to a school that trains oni to fight back. It's a strong pick for fans of action series like Jujutsu Kaisen.
375: Real Bout High School by Reiji Saiga (Tokyopop) is an action comedy set at a very unusual school. At Daimon High, students settle their arguments with official fights called K-Fights. Ryoko Mikado is a kendo champion who has never lost, and she just wants a normal school life. When a mysterious transfer student shows up, things get a lot more complicated. It's a fun read for fans of school fighting stories.
380: Red String by Gina Biggs (Dark Horse) is a heartfelt romance drama. Miharu is a high school girl in Japan who learns that her parents have arranged a marriage for her with a young man she has never met. She is upset, especially since she has her own idea of love. As the two families get to know each other, feelings grow complicated. It's a sweet, emotional pick for readers who love slow-building romance.
386: Death Note Black Edition by Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata (Viz Media) is a dark psychological thriller. Light Yagami is a brilliant high school student who finds a notebook dropped by a death god. Anyone whose name is written in it will die. Light decides to use it to rid the world of criminals, and soon a genius detective known only as L is on his trail. It's a gripping cat-and-mouse story in a handsome collected edition.
387: Demon Love Spell by Mayu Shinjo (Viz Media) is a supernatural romantic comedy. Miko is a shrine maiden who wants to exorcise evil spirits, but she isn't very good at it. When she accidentally seals the powers of Kagura, a handsome and dangerous incubus, he is stuck in a weakened form and sticks around her. The two keep arguing even as their feelings grow. It's a fun pick for fans of fantasy romance.
390: Wild Adapter by Kazuya Minekura (Tokyopop) is a moody crime drama. Makoto Kubota is a laid-back young man who once had ties to the yakuza. One day he picks up Minoru Tokito, a stray with no memory and a strange, beast-like hand. Their meeting pulls them into the mystery of a dangerous drug called Wild Adapter. Gritty and stylish, it's a great choice for fans of Minekura's Saiyuki.
394: Laughing Under the Clouds by Karakara Kemuri (Tokyopop) is a historical action story set in early Meiji-era Japan. The carefree Tenka Kumou and his younger brothers guard prisoners as they are taken to Gokumonjo, a prison on Lake Biwa. Their family is also tied to a legend about the great serpent Orochi, which returns every few hundred years. It's a mix of family warmth and sword fighting, with lovely art.
395: Wonderland by Yugo Ishikawa (Seven Seas) is a survival horror story. Yukko wakes up one morning to find that she and her dog have shrunk to the size of a doll. Her parents have shrunk too, and the familiar world of her house and town has become huge and dangerous. Every ordinary thing could be a threat. It's a tense, creative read for fans of survival stories and strange fantasy.
397: Limit by Keiko Suenobu (Vertical) is a tense survival drama. Mizuki Konno is a high school girl who works hard to fit in with the popular crowd. On a class trip, a bus crash leaves only her and a handful of classmates alive in the woods, with no adults and no way home. As they struggle to survive, the school social order is turned upside down. It's gripping, thoughtful, and sometimes dark.
399: Samurai 8: The Tale of Hachimaru by Masashi Kishimoto (Viz Media) is a sci-fi samurai adventure from the creator of Naruto, with art by Akira Okubo. Hachimaru is a sickly boy who can't survive without life support and dreams of being strong. When a mysterious samurai cat arrives, he gets a chance to become a samurai himself. It's a short, imaginative series for fans of space adventures and big action.
